mercy_translation.text:
For he was not enclosed within the body, nor was he in the body in such a way that he was nowhere else. He did not move the body while the universe was emptied of his activity and providence. Most wonderfully, because he is the Word, he was contained by nothing; rather, he himself contained all things. Just as while present throughout all creation he is outside the universe according to essence yet present in all things by his powers, ordering all things, extending his providence to everything in all things, giving life to each thing and to all together, containing the universe and not being contained, but being wholly and in every respect in his Father alone;

so also, while being in the human body and himself giving it life, he fittingly gave life to the universe as well. He was present in all things and outside all things; and while he was known from the body through his works, he was not absent from the activity of the universe.

It belongs to a soul to contemplate through thought things outside its own body, but not to act outside its own body or move distant things merely by its presence. A human being may think about distant things, but by thinking does not thereby move and transfer them. Nor, if someone sits in his house and thinks about the things in heaven, does he thereby move the sun or turn the heavens. He sees them moving and existing but does not possess the power to operate them.

The Word of God in the human being was not like this. He was not bound to the body; rather, he himself ruled it, so that he was in it and at the same time present in all things, outside existing things, and resting in the Father alone.

And this was the wonder: as a human being he lived a human life; as the Word he gave life to all things; and as Son he was with the Father. Thus when the Virgin gave birth, he himself did not suffer change, nor was he defiled by being in a body; rather, he sanctified the body.

For although he is in all things, he does not share in the nature of all things; rather, all things are given life and nourished by him.

If even the sun, which was made by him and is visible to us, travels through the heavens without being defiled by touching earthly bodies or being hidden by darkness, but instead illuminates and cleanses them, how much more was the all-holy Word of God, the Maker and Lord even of the sun, not defiled when made known in a body. Rather, being incorruptible, he gave life to and purified the mortal body. For Scripture says of him: “He committed no sin, neither was deceit found in his mouth.”

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
Athanasius guards against the idea that the Word is spatially confined by the Incarnation.
The sun analogy illustrates how the holy Word can act through a body without being contaminated by bodily or created limitations.
